evals.name: confirmation gate fires before any search
evals.prompt: Here's my resume (attached). Find me roles that fit.
evals.expected_output: A search brief table with a Source column built from the resume, followed by at most about 5 numbered questions in one message that ask for work mode, base pay floor and visa sponsorship. No job-board request is made before the user answers.
assertions: Shows a search brief table with a Source column (values like resume / inferred / default / needs you)
Asks for work mode, base pay floor, and visa sponsorship
Asks at most about 5 questions, all in one message
Does not run scripts/probe.py (search or --health) before the user replies
Does not ask about or infer age, gender, race, nationality, religion, or family status
Marks the current employer (Lumenly) as an inferred exclusion to confirm

evals.name: remote only, US — non-US remote removed, Americas flagged, employer links
evals.prompt:
Here's my resume (attached). Remote only, and the remote job has to be open to people in the US. No pay floor. I don't need visa sponsorship. Exclude Lumenly. Everything else, use your best read of the resume and go straight to the search.

[Eval setup — not part of the user's message: from the skill folder, run every job-scout script with JOB_SCOUT_REPLAY_DIR=evals/files/worlds/day1 and JOB_SCOUT_HOME set to a new empty temp directory. In Phase 4 run `python3 scripts/probe.py --boards greenhouse:koboldmetals,greenhouse:arizeai,ashby:turquoise-health,ashby:reactivemarkets` instead of the default board pick.]
evals.expected_output: The brief saves work_modes [remote] and remote_scope [US], then the search runs on the four replayed boards. The Reactive Markets Senior Frontend Engineer (Remote, UK) is not in the results table; it may appear under close but excluded with a reason saying remote is limited to the UK. The Kobold Metals Frontend Software Engineer (Remote, North America), if shown, carries an Americas flag. Every link opens the job on the employer's own job page.
assertions: Runs scripts/probe.py with JOB_SCOUT_REPLAY_DIR pointing at evals/files/worlds/day1 and the four-board --boards list
Saves a profile with work_modes ["remote"] and remote_scope including "US"
The Reactive Markets 'Senior Frontend Engineer' (Remote, UK) is not a row in the results table
If the Reactive Markets job is mentioned at all, it is under close but excluded with a reason saying remote is limited to the UK (GB)
If the Kobold Metals 'Frontend Software Engineer' (Remote, North America) is shown, its row or notes carry a flag such as 'Americas — check US eligibility'

Every link in the table is an https employer job page (job-boards.greenhouse.io, jobs.ashbyhq.com or the employer's own site), never an aggregator (Indeed, LinkedIn, ZipRecruiter, Glassdoor and similar) and never an API address
Shows only jobs that scripts/fetch_jd.py reported as open

evals.name: needs sponsorship — refusal quoted or excluded, silence stated
evals.prompt:
Here's my resume (attached). Remote only, open to people in the US. No pay floor. I will need H-1B visa sponsorship, so that's a yes. Exclude Lumenly. Everything else, use your best read of the resume and go straight to the search.

[Eval setup — not part of the user's message: from the skill folder, run every job-scout script with JOB_SCOUT_REPLAY_DIR=evals/files/worlds/day1 and JOB_SCOUT_HOME set to a new empty temp directory. In Phase 4 run `python3 scripts/probe.py --boards greenhouse:koboldmetals,greenhouse:arizeai,ashby:turquoise-health,ashby:reactivemarkets` instead of the default board pick.]
evals.expected_output: The profile saves needs_sponsorship yes. The Turquoise Health Senior Design Engineer description says Turquoise does not sponsor employment visas, so that job is excluded on the sponsorship gate or shown with the refusal quoted word for word. Jobs whose description says nothing about sponsorship (for example the Arize AI Senior Open Source Design Engineer) carry 'sponsorship not stated'. No sponsorship claim appears without a quote.
assertions: Runs scripts/probe.py with JOB_SCOUT_REPLAY_DIR pointing at evals/files/worlds/day1 and the four-board --boards list
Saves the profile with needs_sponsorship "yes"

The Turquoise Health 'Senior Design Engineer' is either left out of the table (and, if mentioned, excluded for sponsorship) or shown with the refusal quoted from its description, e.g. "Turquoise does not sponsor employment visas (H-1B, PERM, etc.)"
Each shown job whose description does not mention sponsorship says 'sponsorship not stated' — it is never described as sponsoring
Every statement that a job does or does not sponsor visas comes with a quote from that job's description
Runs scripts/cite_check.py on results.json and it reports "ok": true before the results are shown

evals.name: just go — proceeds with labelled defaults
evals.prompt: Here's my resume (attached). Skip the questions and just go — use your best guess.
evals.expected_output: The brief is still shown, with every assumed value labelled default (or inferred), and the skill proceeds in the same reply without waiting: it saves the profile and runs the network check.
assertions: Shows the brief table even though the user asked to skip questions
Every value the user did not provide is labelled default or inferred, not presented as confirmed
Does not stop to ask questions
Saves the profile with scripts/state.py profile save and runs scripts/probe.py --health in the same reply
Does not invent a pay floor or a sponsorship answer: base_pay_floor is null (no floor) and needs_sponsorship is undisclosed unless stated

evals.name: negative trigger — cover letter
evals.prompt: Write a cover letter for the Vercel Design Engineer role: https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/vercel/jobs/6129441004
evals.expected_output: No search runs. The reply says cover letters are out of scope for job-scout (or routes outreach to ghostwriter if installed) and offers to find more roles instead.
assertions: Runs no job-scout script (no probe.py, no state.py)
Says cover letters are out of scope for job-scout
Does not draft a cover letter as job-scout output

evals.name: nurse — thin coverage said honestly, no padding
evals.prompt:
Here's my resume (attached). I want nursing roles, onsite or hybrid near Sacramento. No pay floor. I don't need visa sponsorship. Everything else, use your best read of the resume and go straight to the search.

[Eval setup — not part of the user's message: from the skill folder, run every job-scout script with JOB_SCOUT_REPLAY_DIR=evals/files/worlds/day1 and JOB_SCOUT_HOME set to a new empty temp directory. In Phase 4 run `python3 scripts/probe.py --boards greenhouse:koboldmetals,greenhouse:arizeai,ashby:turquoise-health,ashby:reactivemarkets` instead of the default board pick.]
evals.expected_output: The brief says most nursing employers don't use the job boards job-scout reads, so results will be thin. The search runs on the four replayed boards, none of which has a nursing role. The coverage line says coverage was thin for this field. No unrelated roles fill the table. With zero matches, the reply says so and names the filter from filter.py's counts.removed that removed the most jobs.
assertions: Runs scripts/probe.py with JOB_SCOUT_REPLAY_DIR pointing at evals/files/worlds/day1 and the four-board --boards list
Says before searching that coverage for nursing on these job boards is thin
The results' coverage line says coverage was thin for this field
Shows no unrelated roles (software, sales, design or other non-nursing jobs) as matches
If filter.py reports zero candidates, the reply says nothing matched and names the filter with the largest count in filter.py's counts.removed, as shown in the transcript
Does not fall back to web search or aggregator sites

evals.name: chat-only, non-developer user
evals.prompt: I'm a marketing manager in Austin, what's out there?
evals.expected_output: With no resume, the brief is built from the chat (target roles inferred from 'marketing manager', home base Austin from the user). The gate still asks work mode, pay floor and sponsorship. No jargon such as ATS, slug, JSON or API in the questions or brief.
assertions: Builds a brief from the chat message alone; home base Austin has Source you
Still asks for work mode, base pay floor, and visa sponsorship before any search
Does not run scripts/probe.py before the user replies
Uses no jargon (ATS, slug, JSON, API) in the questions or the brief
Mentions honestly that coverage is best for tech and startup employers, if relevant to marketing roles outside tech
